title: Artinian components of a zero-dimensional algebraic space over a field
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and suppose $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is locally of finite type, tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $\dim(X)\le0$. Then $X$ is represented by a separated scheme, every quasi-compact open subscheme of $X$ is affine, and $X$ is a disjoint union of open and closed subschemes $\operatorname{Spec}A_\alpha$ with each $A_\alpha$ a nonzero local Artinian $K$-algebra finite-dimensional as a $K$-vector space. The summands are precisely the one-point connected components. The empty space and an arbitrary, possibly infinite, set of components are allowed. Here separated means that the diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]; open and closed have their scheme meanings [def-weil-open-immersion]. Local means one maximal ideal and Artinian means every descending chain of ideals eventually stabilizes. Dimension for an algebraic space means $\dim(X)=\sup_{x\in|X|}\dim_x(X)$, where $\dim_x(X)=\dim_v(V)$ for any etale scheme chart $V\to X$ and point $v$ over $x$; for a scheme, $\dim_v(V)$ is the infimum of the Krull dimensions of open neighbourhoods of $v$.

source.place: Tag 06LZ (lemma-locally-finite-type-dim-zero), case (2), and varieties.tex Tag 06LH (lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0), locally algebraic case and its proof. The dimension-at-most-zero wording includes the empty space.

proof.text: Take an etale scheme atlas of $X$ and restrict it to affine open charts $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Such charts still cover $X$. By the hypothesis tested on charts, $U$ is locally of finite type over $K$, and by the definition of dimension its dimension is at most zero. Since $U$ is affine it is quasi-compact, so it is of finite type. The affine-finiteness theorem gives $U\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ finite, hence $A$ finite-dimensional over $K$. The zero-dimensional finite-type theorem also gives that $|U|$ is finite. The open-image theorem factors each chart through a representable open subspace $Y\subseteq X$ with a surjective etale atlas $U\to Y$. These $Y$ cover the points of $X$.

source.place: Tag 06LZ, lemma-locally-finite-type-dim-zero, case (2): choose affine charts, applying Tag 06LH to U

proof.text: Fix such a $Y$ and form the scheme $R=U\times_YU$ with projections $s,t$. Representability and etaleness of the atlas imply that both projections are etale. Composing their scheme tests with the atlas gives etale charts $R\to X$; this uses composition of etale scheme maps. Thus $\dim R\le0$. Moreover $R$ is locally of finite type over $K$: on affine pieces the etale projection is locally finitely presented, hence has finitely many algebra generators over the corresponding affine ring of $U$; adjoining generators of that ring over $K$ gives finitely many generators over $K$. Here the chart convention for local finite type applies also after restricting to affine opens of $U$.

source.place: Tag 06LZ, case (2): R is a scheme, etale projections, dimension and local finite type

proof.text: The universal property of the kernel pair makes $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_KU$ a monomorphism: two lifts of the same pair of maps to $U$ agree. It is also a monomorphism on arbitrary field tests, so the field-test criterion for universal injectivity implies that $|j|$ is injective. The affine fibre-product formula identifies $U\times_KU$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_KA)$. If $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ span $A$ over $K$, the $a_i\otimes a_j$ span its tensor square. Hence that algebra is finite-dimensional, therefore Artinian, and its prime spectrum is finite. The injection just obtained proves $|R|$ finite, without assuming the relation quasi-compact or $X$ quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 06LZ, case (2): the finite(!) union argument; Tags 01S4, 01I4, 00J6 and 00J7 spell out finiteness

proof.text: A finite topological space is quasi-compact: choose one covering member per point. Thus $R$, already locally of finite type over $K$, is of finite type. Since $\dim R\le0$, the affine-finiteness theorem makes $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite-dimensional over $K$. Each projection $R\to U$ is finite: a finite $K$-spanning list of $B$ also generates $B$ as an $A$-module for either of the two $K$-algebra maps $A\to B$, since its $K$-linear coefficients are images of elements of $A$. The maps are affine maps between affines, so this is precisely the finiteness criterion. Etaleness supplies flatness and local finite presentation. Therefore both projections are finite locally free, with that term understood as finite, flat and locally finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 06LZ, case (2): R affine and finite over K; finite projections; preparation for Tag 03BM

proof.text: For every test scheme $T$, the maps $(s,t)$ identify $R(T)$ with the equivalence relation on $U(T)$ given by equality in $Y(T)$. Apply the affine finite-locally-free relation quotient theorem over $\operatorname{Spec}K$: its fppf quotient is an affine scheme $M$. It represents $Y$ as well. Indeed $U\to Y$ has fppf local lifts; any section of $Y$ can locally be represented by a map to $U$. Two such representatives agree in $Y$ exactly when their pair is a section of $R$. Thus maps from the orbit presheaf into any fppf sheaf extend uniquely across $Y$, by sheaf gluing and the same local-lift argument. This is the universal property of its fppf sheafification, which $M$ also satisfies. Hence $Y\simeq h_M$; Yoneda interprets the resulting representable-sheaf identification as the scheme identification when required.

source.place: Tag 06LZ, end of case (2), using groupoids.tex Tag 03BM, proposition-finite-flat-equivalence

proof.text: The largest schematic open $X_{\mathrm{sch}}\subseteq X$ contains every open $Y$ just proved affine. Their point sets cover $|X|$, so this open has full point image. The point/open calculus says that an open subspace with full point image equals $X$. Consequently $X$ is a scheme. All constructions retain their $K$-structures. No global finite-type, quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness hypothesis was introduced.

source.place: Tag 06LZ, opening local-to-global reduction; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03JH, lemma-subscheme

proof.text: For any quasi-compact open subscheme $V\subseteq X$, restriction preserves local finite type (restrict the affine charts in its definition). The dimension bound restricts to an open subspace. Hence $V$ is of finite type over $K$ with dimension at most zero, and the affine-finiteness theorem makes it affine and finite over $K$. Apply the finite-type zero-dimensional topology theorem to affine open charts of $X$: each has discrete topology. A subset of $X$ is open exactly when its intersections with these open charts are open, so $X$ is discrete. This gives both the requested affineness assertion and the open-and-closed nature of each singleton.

source.place: Tag 06LH, lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0, first two paragraphs; Tag 06LZ affineness assertion

proof.text: For $x\in|X|$, let $C_x$ be the open singleton subscheme. It is quasi-compact, so the preceding argument gives $C_x=\operatorname{Spec}A_x$ finite over $K$. Thus $A_x$ is finite-dimensional over $K$, and is Artinian by the finite-dimensional-algebra theorem. It is nonzero because its spectrum is nonempty. It is local: every maximal ideal is prime, and its spectrum has exactly one prime, so it has exactly one maximal ideal. This uses no algebraic-closedness or reducedness hypothesis on $K$ or $X$.

source.place: Tag 06LH, second paragraph: singleton components and their local Artinian finite algebras

proof.text: Form the scheme coproduct $D=\coprod_{x\in|X|}C_x$. The component inclusions give a morphism $D\to X$. Conversely the inverse identity maps $C_x\to D$ glue over the disjoint open cover of $X$; compatibility on overlaps is vacuous. Morphism gluing shows that the two composites restrict to the identity on every component and hence are identities globally. Therefore $D\simeq X$. A singleton is connected, while any subset of a discrete space containing distinct points is disconnected by splitting off one point. Thus these are precisely the connected components. The empty index set and any infinite set are allowed by the coproduct theorem.

source.place: Tag 06LH, second paragraph: disjoint union of singleton connected components

proof.text: Use the singleton affine open cover to apply the separated affine-cover criterion with base $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Distinct members have empty intersection, which is $\operatorname{Spec}0$, and the corresponding ring map to the zero ring is surjective. For a member intersected with itself the restriction map is multiplication $A_x\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A_x\to A_x$, which is surjective since $a$ is the image of $a\otimes1$. Hence the absolute diagonal is a closed immersion. This proves separatedness in exactly the sense asserted, including for an infinite coproduct (the cover need not be finite) and the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 06LZ, opening assertion that X is separated; schemes.tex Tag 01KP, lemma-characterize-separated

proof_origin.place: Tag 06LZ, lemma-locally-finite-type-dim-zero, proof of (2); Tag 06LH, lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0, locally algebraic clause and proof. Kernel-pair finiteness and absolute separatedness expanded explicitly.

The route differs slightly from the source: each affine étale chart's open image Y=X_f is shown affine as U/R, with R=U×_YU. In detail, |R| is finite because R→U×_KU is a monomorphism and the field-point criterion (01S4) applies, with Spec(A⊗_KA) finite-dimensional and so Artinian with finite spectrum. Then R=Spec B is finite over K and s,t are finite locally free. The 03BM quotient lemma applies, its hypotheses checked, and the local-lifting gluing argument identifies Y with the sheafified U/R. The largest schematic open (03JH) plus the point/open calculus then show X is a scheme. From there: qc opens are affine and finite (06LH), X is discrete, singleton components are nonzero local Artinian finite-dimensional algebras, D=⨿C_x≅X by coproduct and gluing, and separatedness over Z follows from the 01KP criterion (empty and multiplication maps surjective). Edge cases tested: empty X, K[ε]/ε², a purely inseparable extension, and an infinite coproduct. The six declared tool uses are accepted as generic scheme and algebraic-space foundations. The 03BM quotient reaches only lem-trf-finite-presentation-module-descent-flat-local, which is pure faithfully-flat module descent. All four are accepted. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem zeroDimensional_fieldSpace_components {K : Type u} [Field K] (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) (hft : ∀ (U : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale p → LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom) (hdim : ∀ (U : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale p → ∀ v : U.left, (⨅ (W : U.left.Opens) (_ : v ∈ W), topologicalKrullDim W) ≤ 0) : ∃ Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)), Nonempty (yoneda.obj Y ≅ X.obj.obj) ∧ IsClosedImmersion (prod.lift (𝟙 Y.left) (𝟙 Y.left)) ∧ (∀ V : Y.left.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set Y.left) → IsAffine V.toScheme) ∧ ∃ (I : Type u) (A : I → CommAlgCat.{u} K) (ι : ∀ i : I, Spec (CommRingCat.of (A i)) ⟶ Y.left), Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk Y.left ι)) ∧ (∀ i : I, Nontrivial (A i) ∧ IsLocalRing (A i) ∧ IsArtinianRing (A i) ∧ FiniteDimensional K (A i) ∧ ι i ≫ Y.hom = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (A i))) ∧ IsOpenImmersion (ι i) ∧ IsClosed (Set.range (ι i)) ∧ Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of (A i)))) ∧ ∀ x : Y.left, ∃! i : I, Set.range (ι i) = connectedComponent x
